solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: I doubt that bacon supplier's hoping to export

definitions.meaning: a scornful retort meaning something will never happen
read literally: the animals that give us bacon may take to the air, as if hoping to send themselves abroad

explanation.surface: A sceptic scoffs at a pork producer's plans to sell bacon overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: the bacon supplier is the pig itself, which might take wing.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom expresses complete disbelief that something will ever happen.

clue.text: Inconstant dull performance? Be critical of including that

indicators.note: the critical word holds the dull performance within it

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly
rote is mechanical, routine repetition

explanation.surface: A reviewer is asked to slam a fickle, dreary show.
explanation.definitionFit: Protean means ever-changing, like the shape-shifting sea god Proteus.

clue.text: Good form, embodying an example of hardness

indicators.note: the form word takes the little word into its body

parts.note: a rite is a set form of ceremony

explanation.surface: Good form embodies something tough, like a character reference.
explanation.definitionFit: Granite is a very hard rock, a byword for toughness.

clue.text: TV and newspapers intend to get upset about fool going to sea

indicators.note: the turned word goes around the other pieces
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word reads from the bottom

parts.note: to aim is to intend
an ass is a fool
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: Someone means to complain about an idiot heading off on a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'to get upset' reads the intend word upwards; 'about' then wraps it round the other two pieces. 'going to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Television and the press are the main forms of mass communication.

clue.text: Banned from university degree, receiving cheers when that's reversed

indicators.note: the whole combination is then read backwards
the degree abbreviation takes in the thanks

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks

explanation.surface: A student denied a degree is consoled with cheers, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' gives DETAG, which 'when that's reversed' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: At Oxford and Cambridge a student who is gated is confined to college as a punishment.

clue.text: Ruin of journalist overcome by unending apathy

indicators.note: in a down clue the journalist sits beneath, inside, the shortened word
the apathy word loses its final letter

parts.note: torpor is lethargy or apathy
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter's downfall comes from endless indifference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unending' trims TORPOR to TORPO, which holds ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To torpedo a plan is to wreck or sink it, a verb sense of ruin.

clue.text: Working together with Independent to probe absence of rigging that's arisen

indicators.note: the single letter pokes into the reversed phrase
in a down clue, rising means the phrase reads upwards

parts.note: no sail describes a boat stripped of its canvas

explanation.surface: An Independent investigates a missing ship's rigging scandal that has surfaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's arisen' turns NO SAIL into LIASON; 'to probe' pushes I into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is cooperation or communication between parties, the noun sense of joint working.

clue.text: A demonstration that nothing can cure you?

definitions.text: A demonstration that nothing can cure you?

parts.words: A demonstration that nothing can cure you?
parts.note: a dummy pill with no active ingredient can still make a patient feel better, so 'nothing' cures

explanation.surface: It sounds like a gloomy diagnosis that no treatment will work.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'nothing can cure you' as an inert substance healing you, not as hopelessness.
explanation.definitionFit: The phenomenon is improvement in a patient caused by a sham treatment and belief alone.

clue.text: Raving bonkers to go round a rugged part of Yorkshire

indicators.note: the jumbled letters wrap around the single letter
raving means wild and mad, so the letters go haywire

parts.note: rough means rugged

explanation.surface: Someone crazy is told to tour a wild stretch of Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raving' signals the jumble and 'to go round' places the single letter inside it; 'rugged' is the last piece, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Knaresborough is a market town in North Yorkshire, near Harrogate.

clue.text: Overturned mug has spoiled things in bathroom

indicators.note: the word for the dupe is turned back to front

parts.note: a mug is a gullible person, a fool

indicators.note: spoiled means messed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A knocked-over mug has made a mess of things in the bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overturned' turns FOOL into LOOF; 'spoiled' mixes HAS into AHS. 'mug' is a person, not a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Loofahs are fibrous gourd sponges used for scrubbing in the bath.

clue.text: Soccer club employee has little hesitation moving ground

indicators.note: the hesitation letters shift to a new place within the employee's title

parts.note: a football club employs a trainer
er is a short hesitant noise

explanation.surface: A football coach hesitates briefly before moving onto the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is land or ground considered by its physical features.

clue.text: About to think about passing current through metal

parts.note: CA stands for circa, about

indicators.note: the current goes into the reversed word
the current runs right through the middle of the reversed word
here about means turned round, so the pondering word reads backwards

parts.note: to muse is to ponder
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An electrician muses about running a current through some metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses MUSE to ESUM; 'passing ... through' puts I in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesium is a soft alkali metal, element 55.

clue.text: Item of furniture a fixture backstage?

definitions.meaning: a sideboard with shelves for dishes
a theatre assistant who helps actors into costume is a regular presence behind the scenes

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture permanently fixed behind a theatre stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixture' suggests a fitted object, but it means a person always there.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a kitchen cupboard with shelves and a theatre wardrobe assistant.

clue.text: Quantity of wine, say, knocked back in this

definitions.text: Quantity of wine, say, knocked back in this

parts.note: a bin is a cellar rack or stock of bottled wine

indicators.note: the example abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: eg, for example, is signalled by say

explanation.surface: A lot of wine, for instance, gets downed during a heavy session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' reverses EG to GE; the whole clue also describes a drinking spree.
explanation.definitionFit: A binge is a bout of excessive drinking, when much wine is swallowed.

clue.text: Has a meal, swallowing some cooking in US city

indicators.note: the eating word takes in the other letters

parts.note: dines means has a meal

indicators.note: cooking suggests letters being worked into a new mix

explanation.surface: Someone eats a meal, wolfing down some home cooking in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' signals the jumble and 'swallowing' puts it inside the eating word, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Des Moines is the state capital of Iowa.

clue.text: Main store failing to provide household item

indicators.note: a failing store is in disarray, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A department store collapses and stops supplying household goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam iron is a domestic appliance for pressing clothes.

clue.text: Pale sand piled up beyond far side of here?

definitions.text: Pale sand piled up beyond far side of here?

indicators.note: sand heaped in disorder means the letters are jumbled
the far side of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Light sand heaped up on the other side of a seaside place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beyond' places the final letter of 'here' after the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A seafront promenade lies just beyond the beach where sand piles up.

clue.text: Old King, a King enthralled by power and sudden pronouncements

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power

indicators.note: held captive inside the exclamations

parts.note: ha and oh are exclamations, sudden utterances
R is for Rex, king

explanation.surface: An ancient ruler, enchanted by power, makes abrupt declarations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enthralled by' puts A and R between the H and A of HA OH.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharaoh was a ruler of ancient Egypt, so a king of old.

clue.text: Article with lines about this reduced agglomeration of workers?

indicators.note: the article and lines go around the shortened word

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
L is the abbreviation for line, so LL is lines

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A newspaper article and some lines on how this has been cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the article and lines around the trimmed word. The question mark flags that 'workers' are worker ants.
explanation.definitionFit: An ant colony's mound is a heap of insect workers, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Odd thing identified by copper meeting small group without leader

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: the group loses its first letter

parts.note: a trio is a group of three

explanation.surface: A policeman spots something strange with a small leaderless band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' is the element, not a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A curio is a rare or unusual object, a curiosity.

clue.text: Be a success? Astonished comment won't accept it

indicators.note: the exclamation refuses to take the little word, so it is removed

parts.note: come off it is an incredulous retort

explanation.surface: Someone stunned exclaims they won't believe a claimed success.
explanation.definitionFit: To come off is to work out as planned, a phrasal verb for succeeding.

clue.text: Work for Brazilian mayor? Time to go wild

parts.note: a mayor of Rio de Janeiro would run Rio

explanation.surface: A city mayor in Brazil says it is time to let loose, carnival-style.
explanation.definitionFit: To run riot is to behave wildly and without restraint, an idiom.

clue.text: Wild diatribe applied to one in soccer team

indicators.note: the tirade and numeral go inside the club letters

parts.note: FC, football club, is a soccer team
a rant is a bitter tirade
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A furious tirade is aimed at one player in a football side.
explanation.definitionFit: Frantic means frenzied, out of control with worry or excitement.

clue.text: Generator of buzz about to turn up, handling opening of library?

definitions.text: Generator of buzz about to turn up, handling opening of library?

parts.note: C stands for circa, about

indicators.note: the insect holds the letter inside it
in a down clue turning up means the letters read upwards

parts.note: a bee makes a buzzing noise

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A buzzing insect turns up to open a new library.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handling' gives BELE; with C after it, 'to turn up' reverses BELEC. A famous guest generates buzz.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity creates excitement and media chatter, for instance at a library opening.

clue.text: Blokes invested in largely imitative souvenir

indicators.note: placed inside, as money is put into a venture
most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: me-too describes copycat products
blokes are men

explanation.surface: Men put money into a copycat keepsake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' cuts METOO to METO, and 'invested in' puts MEN in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is a keepsake kept to remember a person or event.

clue.text: Persuade island to take exposed half of cable

parts.note: to coax is to persuade gently

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of its outer layer, leaving the middle letters

explanation.surface: Coaxing an island to accept half a cable with bare wires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposed half' looks like the middle of cable, but 'half' itself is stripped to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Coaxial describes cable with a central conductor inside a tubular one sharing an axis.

clue.text: Covering investment of money in boxing

indicators.note: money goes into the boxing word, as funds are invested in it

parts.note: the ring is the sport of boxing, by metonymy
oof is old slang for money

explanation.surface: Insurance cover for money put into professional boxing.
explanation.definitionFit: Roofing is material laid to cover a building's top.

clue.text: Church re-envisaged life in debt with support for young

indicators.note: imagined afresh, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: The church reimagines a life in debt, helping the young.
explanation.walkthrough: Child Benefit is a UK state payment to parents for each child.
explanation.definitionFit: This British welfare payment gives financial help to families raising children.
